picks.what: Engraving in Tournefort’s Relation d’un voyage du Levant
picks.why: labeled “Tiflis, Capitale de Géorgie”; walled Narikala fortress above the town

picks.file: Vue de Tiflis (1830s), Engelmann, after Louis Firmin Le Camus.jpg
picks.who: Godefroy Engelmann after Louis Firmin Le Camus
picks.why: Narikala fortress, the Kura and the town spread below; larger copy of the same plate as #3

picks.file: Town and fortress, Tiflis, Russia, (Tbilisi, Georgia)-LCCN2001697511.jpg
picks.what: The fortress and the town, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: color general view from above: Narikala walls, the Kura and the whole town

picks.file: 471 - Panorama of the old city and the fortress of Tbilisi.jpg
picks.what: The old town and the Kura from above, photograph
picks.why: color view over the old town, the river and the Metekhi cliff, with the fortress hill at right

picks.what: Panorama of the city with the Holy Trinity Cathedral, photograph
picks.why: sharp panorama of the whole city with the Holy Trinity Cathedral and the Kura

notes: #1: Commons dates it 1701, the year of Tournefort’s visit (drawing by Claude Aubriet); the plate was first published in the Relation d’un voyage du Levant, 1717, so y is 1717. #11 (Paul von Franken painting, 1859, very large) is a strong alternative for P4 but only 36 years from the photochrom, and its foreground genre scene dominates. #19 (1918, German expedition) and #14 (1914–18) are black and white with foreground figures or a single church; the 1964 color view was preferred for P5. #12 (Prokudin-Gorskii, Havlabar) has no exact year.
